_why: Ground truth for the fingerprint: would a stranger say these two came from
one tool, or from two different studios?
Judged BLIND, from the first-viewport screenshots alone, with no axis
values in view. The first version of this file was contaminated — four of
four 'different' verdicts were justified in the vector's own vocabulary
(mood, accent, layout bias, leads-with), so agreement was measuring the
instrument against a restatement of itself. Every `why` below describes
what is on the screen. If a verdict cannot be written that way it is not a
judgement about the picture.
The rule that resolves the near-ties: a difference in COLOUR or SUBJECT
alone is not a different site. Two pages that share a skeleton, a type
treatment and a first screen are the same site painted twice, whatever the
accent and whoever is in the photograph.
A difference in how the name is SET — its size, its case, the spacing of
its letters — is not by itself a different site either, and for the same
reason. The words differ between any two businesses, so the lettering
always differs; what a stranger recognises is the arrangement, and a
setting applied to the same arrangement is the same page in another font.
It counts only when it MOVES the type somewhere else on the screen, or
changes what shares the screen with it — that is a change of arrangement
rather than of setting.
Written 2026-09-08, before looking at which verdicts it moves, because the
two it was written to resolve contradict each other and whichever way it
is stated it decides one of them. The gap it fills: the rule above names
colour and subject and is silent on type setting, and two verdicts fell
into that silence in opposite directions.

_judged_against: The rendering as of page architecture landing — distance ruler aece36b7, gate rule 95f4d93e — read off .reviews/sheet, half-scale pictures of the desktop FIRST VIEWPORT, which is the method and which is the problem this round found: an axis that lives below the fold cannot be judged from a picture of the fold.
_held_out: One verdict in three, chosen by a hash of the two slugs so that nobody picks which evidence survives. A held-out verdict is never used to choose a rule or a weighting, only to score one afterwards, and it is never re-judged — when the page under it changes it is retired with a reason and the set gets smaller. It starts here, so it says nothing about the rule this commit lands: the first rule it can honestly score is the next one.
_retired: A retired verdict is scored by nothing and re-judged by nobody. Retiring is what happens to a held-out pair when the page under it changes, and to any pair whose subject turns out not to be judgeable — the set shrinks, which is the honest cost of the number meaning anything.
